Definition: neuter of a compound of G5259 and G4228; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively):--footstool.
BiblicalUsage: The word hypopódion carries the sense of footstool. In Matthew 5:35, the text says "for it is his footstool." In Luke 20:43, the text says "Till I make thine enemies thy footstool."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hypopódion tells me that Christ is King now, not only one day, and His rule is good news for His people. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Pentecost; The Sermon on the Mount
